question: What is a primary goal of immunization in community settings?

options.A: Achieving herd immunity and preventing diseases

explanation: Community immunization aims to protect populations by preventing vaccine-preventable diseases and building community-wide immunity. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h1)

question: Why is engagement with local leaders important during community outreach?

options.A: To collect taxes for the health facility
options.B: To address vaccine hesitancy and build trust

explanation: Collaborating with local and traditional leaders helps foster community trust, encourage participation, and address vaccine hesitancy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h1)

question: Which vaccine must be strictly protected from freezing during field storage?
explanation: Tetanus toxoid and hepatitis B vaccines can be permanently damaged and lose potency if subjected to freezing temperatures. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) on a vaccine label?

options.A: To indicate the exact manufacturing date
options.B: To show if the vaccine has been exposed to excessive heat
options.C: To measure the exact volume of liquid remaining
options.D: To determine the batch or lot number of the drug

explanation: A VVM changes color to indicate cumulative heat exposure, helping the nurse determine if the vaccine is safe to use. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h2)

question: Which of the following is generally considered a true contraindication to vaccination?

options.A: Mild upper respiratory tract infection with low-grade fever
options.B: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine
options.C: Mild diarrhea lasting less than twenty-four hours
options.D: Local soreness at a previous injection site

explanation: A history of a severe anaphylactic reaction to a previous dose is a definitive contraindication to receiving subsequent doses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h3)

question: Why should live attenuated vaccines be used with extreme caution in immunocompromised clients?

options.A: They cause severe injection site abscesses
options.B: They can replicate uncontrollably and cause severe disease
options.C: They are completely inactivated and lack any effectiveness
options.D: They interact poorly with routine oral analgesics

explanation: Immunocompromised individuals cannot effectively fight off live organisms, making live attenuated vaccines potentially dangerous for them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h3)

question: What is the preferred anatomical site for an intramuscular vaccine injection in an infant?
explanation: The vastus lateralis in the anterolateral thigh is well-developed in infants and provides a safe site away from major nerves and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h4)

question: Why are auto-disable (AD) syringes used during immunization sessions?

options.A: They allow multiple doses to be drawn from one vial easily
options.B: They lock automatically to prevent reuse after a single injection
options.C: They reduce the overall cost of community outreach programs
options.D: They eliminate the need for sharps disposal containers

explanation: Auto-disable syringes render themselves unusable after a single injection, effectively preventing accidental reuse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of community mobilization before an outreach session?

options.A: To inspect the cold chain equipment for technical faults
options.B: To inform the populace and maximize turnout and coverage
options.C: To distribute routine medical drugs for chronic illnesses
options.D: To construct temporary health clinic structures

explanation: Community mobilization informs residents about the upcoming immunization program, encouraging high attendance and better coverage rates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h5)

question: Why is an organized spatial flow important during an outreach vaccination session?

options.A: It helps manage crowds and reduces waiting times for clients
options.B: It allows the nurse to administer vaccines without gloves
options.C: It eliminates the need for any pre-vaccination screening
options.D: It ensures that only adult clients are vaccinated first

explanation: An orderly flow from registration to observation ensures efficiency, reduces chaos, and keeps clients moving smoothly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h5)

question: How is an Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI) broadly defined?

options.A: Only events proven to be caused by the vaccine's active ingredients
options.B: Any untoward medical occurrence following immunization regardless of causality
options.C: Any local swelling that lasts longer than seven days post-injection
options.D: Reactions that occur exclusively within five minutes of vaccine administration

explanation: An AEFI is any medical incident following vaccination, whether or not it is directly caused by the vaccine itself. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h6)

question: What type of AEFI is caused by incorrect handling, reconstitution, or administration technique?
explanation: Errors in preparation, handling, or administration by the healthcare provider fall under immunization error-related reactions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the personal immunization card given to a child's caregiver?

options.A: To serve as proof of age for school enrollment
options.B: To act as a lifelong health record tracking immunization history
options.C: To qualify the family for government financial assistance
options.D: To serve as a tally sheet for the community health worker

explanation: The immunization card tracks the child's vaccine doses over time, ensuring continuity of care across different health facilities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h7)

question: When should tally sheets be filled out during a community immunization session?

options.A: In real-time as each vaccine dose is administered
options.B: At the end of the week from memory
options.C: Before the session begins based on expected turnout
options.D: Only when requested by district supervisors

explanation: Real-time recording on tally sheets prevents omissions and ensures accurate documentation of administered doses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h7)
